Reasons for Submitting the Bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this Bill is to guarantee legal protection for the right to protection of name and reputation afforded to every person under Article 33 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives; to establish an appropriate balance between the right to freedom of expression in society and the protection and preservation of the reputation of individuals; to state that a party who has been defamed has the right to have the truth of the matter disclosed, or to reply, or to have the matter corrected; and, in addition, to determine that defamation is a civil wrong, to set out what constitutes defamation, the circumstances that shall not be deemed defamation and the circumstances in which privilege is afforded, and to set out all the principles and standards for seeking an apology from the party who defames, for making an offer of compensation, for a defamed party to file a case in court to seek compensation for the damage suffered, and for the award of compensation for damage.

Right to Protection of Name and Reputation Bill

Chapter One
Preliminary Articles

Introduction and Title
1. (a) This is an Act to set out, in a manner by which the right to have one's name and reputation protected, afforded to every person under Article 33 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, can be enforced in practice, the legal protection to be afforded under that right; to set out the standard for determining defamation and the circumstances that shall not be deemed defamation; to determine that defamation is a civil wrong; and to set out the legal remedies available to a defamed party as a result of defamation and all other related principles.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Right to Protection of Name and Reputation Act".

Purpose
2. The purpose of this Act is to achieve the following.

(a) Whereas the right of persons to have their name and reputation protected is guaranteed under Article 33 of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, to take legal measures in order not to allow that right to be

[stamp] [signature]

(b) This Act shall apply to all of the following productions.

(1) Statements made in writing or orally, and statements made in visual and/or audio form;

(2) Material of every kind that is broadcast, printed or published online;

(3) Any other means by which a statement is made or disseminated in a manner that communicates it to, or allows it to reach, any third party.

(c) This Act shall not apply to a private communication between two parties, if that communication was held solely in a private manner and is not disclosed to any third party. However, if such a communication reaches or is disseminated to any third party or the public by any means, that communication shall fall within the scope of this Act.

(d) This Act shall apply to all of the following acts.

(1) All acts of defamation committed within the territory of the Maldives; and

(2) All acts of defamation committed outside the territory of the Maldives

[stamp] [signature]

in the following circumstances.

i. The defamatory statement being available in the Maldives; and

ii. It being deemed, on the basis of reasonable grounds, that as a result thereof the reputation of a party in the Maldives has been damaged or may be damaged.

(e) Even if an act specified in subsection (d) of this Article was committed wholly or to any extent outside the territory of the Maldives, the courts of the Maldives shall have jurisdiction over such acts.

Chapter Two
Right to Protection of Name and Reputation

Scope of the Right to Protection of Name and Reputation
5. (a) Every person has the right to legal protection against unlawful attacks on that person's name and reputation. And every person has the right to seek compensation for damage suffered as a result of defamation.

(b) If damage is caused to the name and reputation of any person by an act committed unlawfully or by negligence, the State shall establish, in accordance with this Act, an easily accessible system through which appropriate legal remedies may be obtained.

[stamp] [signature]

(c) In exercising the right to protection of name and reputation, that right shall not be interpreted or applied in a manner that restricts lawful expression, debate and criticism to an unreasonable extent.

Duty to Respect the Rights of Others
6. (a) Every person shall exercise the freedom of expression afforded to him under Article 27 of the Constitution in accordance with Article 67 of the Constitution, in a responsible manner, safeguarding the rights, freedoms and reputation of others, and with full respect for those rights, freedoms and reputation.

(b) The media, digital platforms and other parties engaged in the work of publication shall maintain a standard of reasonable care in order to ensure the accuracy, fairness and credibility of the information disseminated through their platforms.

(c) The media, digital platforms and other parties engaged in the work of publication shall establish and implement appropriate mechanisms for promptly correcting, clarifying or withdrawing information provided by them, if it becomes known that such information is false or misleading.

(d) By acting in accordance with this Article, that party being deemed to be absolved from a responsibility imposed upon any person or party under other Articles of this Act

[stamp] [signature]

shall not be permitted.

Right of Reply
7. A defamed party has the right to have the truth of the defamatory matter disclosed, or to reply to it, or to have the matter corrected.

Chapter Three
Defamation

Determination of the Wrong
8. Defamation is a civil wrong. And every party defamed as a result of defamation has the right to seek and obtain the solutions or remedies determined in this Act.

Defamation
9. In this Act, "defamation" means the commission by another party, intentionally or without reasonable care, against a particular party or in relation to a particular party, of an act among the following acts.

(a) Attributing a false statement to a particular party, or giving or publishing false information, or committing an act by which false information is obtained; and

(b) As a result of making that false statement, or giving or publishing false information, or committing an act by which that information is obtained, an adverse change occurring in the respect shown towards, or in the regard held of, the party to whom that statement or information was attributed in the minds of right-thinking members of society; or hatred towards that party being brought about; or, as a result of that statement or of what was published,

[stamp] [signature]

(5) Through objects made in the form of something attributable to a particular person or in a manner depicting a person, or by a film made, or through things such as stage shows and dramatic performances; or

(6) Something defamatory of a particular party coming to be portrayed, conceived, understood or known as a result of gestures made, movements made or any other act committed.

(b) If, through an act specified in subsection (a) of this Article, the reputation of a person is impugned, whether directly and explicitly or indirectly, it shall be deemed defamation for the purposes of this Act.

Standard for Determining Defamation
11. (a) For the purposes of this Act, a particular party shall be deemed to have been defamed if the following conditions are fulfilled in relation to an act specified in Article 10 of this Act.

(1) The statement made or the information given being a false statement or false information;

(2) The statement made or the information given being something that has been made public;

(3) The statement made or the information given being a statement or information attributable to the defamed party.

(b) For the purposes of subsection (a)(1) of this Article, however damaging the statement

[stamp] [signature]

or the information given may be to the reputation of the defamed party, if it is true, it shall not be deemed an act of defamation.

(c) For the purposes of subsection (a)(2) of this Article, the following principles shall apply in determining whether a statement made or information given has been made public.

(1) If it is proven that the statement made or the information given was not a statement made or information given with the intention of making it public, that statement or information shall not be deemed to have been made public.

(2) Notwithstanding subsection (c)(1) of this Article, if it is reasonable to believe that the statement or information may reach a third party, that statement or information shall be deemed to have been made public. Accordingly, a statement or information shall be deemed to have been made public in the following circumstances.

i. The statement having been made or the information having been given to, or in the presence of, a third party other than the defamed party; or

ii. The statement or the information given being a writing, statement, photograph, video, song or other information published in a book, newspaper or magazine, or broadcast through radio, television

[stamp] [signature]

to believe, from the words or information used, that it refers to the defamed party, that statement or information shall be deemed to be attributable to the defamed party.

Defamation through the Internet
12. (a) Nothing defamatory of a particular party shall be published or included in a writing disclosed using the internet, or on a website prepared and operated, or on social media, or in an online newspaper issued, or in a blog, or in any other thing or means made public through the internet.

(b) The party who wrote, published or disclosed a defamatory thing specified in subsection (a) of this Article, or parties who disseminate such a thing to further parties, shall bear responsibility for it under this Act. And if the defamatory thing was written, published or disclosed in a newspaper operated online, the responsible party and the editor of that newspaper and/or the owner of that website shall bear responsibility under this Act.

(c) For the purposes of this Article, internet service providers shall not be required to bear responsibility under this Act.

(d) A defamatory thing shall be deemed to have been made public in the Maldives through the internet in the following circumstances.

(1) The defamatory thing having been uploaded, downloaded or

[stamp] [signature]

read through the internet in the Maldives; or

(2) The defamed party being a Maldivian citizen, or a party residing or established in the Maldives.

Circumstances that Shall Not Be Deemed Defamation
13. If any of the following circumstances exists in an act alleged to be defamation, that act shall not be deemed an act of defamation under this Act.

(a) The statement made or the information given in attribution to a person being the true fact; or

(b) The statement made or the information given in attribution to a person being an opinion or view based on the true facts.

Being True Information
14. In a defamation action filed under this Act, if the party accused of defamation proves to the court that the statement made or the information given is entirely the true fact, the court shall not deem that statement or that information to be defamatory.

Expression of Honest Opinion or View
15. In a defamation action filed under this Act, if the party accused of defamation proves to the court that the statement made or the information given is a statement made or information given in the following circumstances, the court shall not deem that statement or that information to be defamatory.

(a) Instead of stating definitively that it is the truth of a matter, it

[stamp] [signature]

being a disclosure of that person's own honest opinion or view, and it having been specifically stated, when disclosing that statement or information, that it is a disclosure of that person's own honest opinion or view; and

(b) The party accused of defamation believing in good faith that the opinion or view is an opinion or view based on true facts; and

(c) The opinion or view being something based on true information available in a manner permitted by law.

Permissible Defence
16. In addition to the matters specified in Article 13 of this Act, the following matters or circumstances are permissible defences that may be used by the party accused of defamation in defence of a defamation action.

(a) The statement being a statement made, or the information being information made public, with the knowledge and consent of the defamed party;

(b) Other matters specified in the regulation made under this Act.

Formulation of Standards on Acts of Defamation
17. For the purpose of the court determining which acts may and may not be deemed acts of defamation, a detailed standard relating to such matters shall be set out in the regulation made under this Act, in a manner not inconsistent with the standards set out in this Chapter. In particular, the following matters shall be determined in that

[stamp] [signature]

privilege.

(b) If the statement made or the information given is a statement made or information given in a circumstance specified in Articles 19 and 20 of this Act, no action may be brought under this Act against the party accused of defamation in that circumstance.

Privilege Afforded to Members of the People's Majlis
19. (a) Even if something defamatory of a particular party is said in a speech made by a member of the People's Majlis at a lawful sitting of the People's Majlis or at an official meeting of a committee of that Majlis, it shall not be deemed an act of defamation for the purposes of this Act.

(b) Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this Article, if a member of the People's Majlis makes a statement or gives information defamatory of a particular party outside a sitting of the People's Majlis or a committee meeting, that member shall bear responsibility for it under this Act.

(c) The broadcasting of a lawful sitting of the People's Majlis or an official meeting of a committee of that Majlis shall not be deemed an act of defamation for the purposes of this Act.

(d) Even if something defamatory of a particular party is included in a document published by the People's Majlis, or in expressions contained in a report setting out the proceedings of that Majlis or of a committee of that Majlis, or in part of such document or report, the publication or making public of such document or

[stamp] [signature]

report shall not be deemed an act of defamation for the purposes of this Act.

Judicial Privilege
20. The inclusion of something defamatory of a particular party in a statement given or a document submitted, in a court hearing or session being held in relation to a matter proceeding before a court or tribunal, by a judge or tribunal member hearing that matter, or by a litigant, or a legal counsel, or a witness, or an expert, or any other party involved in the matter, shall not be deemed an act of defamation for the purposes of this Act.

Privilege Afforded Subject to Conditions
21. (a) If the statement made or the information given is a statement made or information given in a circumstance specified in Article 22 of this Act, the parties accused of defamation in that circumstance are afforded privilege subject to conditions.

(b) If the statement made or the information given is a statement made or information given in a circumstance specified in Article 22 of this Act, no action may be brought under this Act against the party accused of defamation in that circumstance.

Conditions to be Fulfilled to Obtain Privilege
22. Privilege shall be afforded to any party under Article 21 of this Act only if the following conditions are fulfilled.

(a) It being believed, with honest

[stamp] [signature]

Directors of any public company operating in the Maldives, or a document issued by the auditors of the company, or a document issued under a legal power vested in a member of the company, or part of such document; and

(n) Disclosing, as it stands and without addition or omission, a document issued by any public company operating in the Maldives relating to the appointment, removal or retirement of directors of that company or to a proposal for their resignation, or part of such document.

Non-Granting of Privilege in Matters Involving the Public Interest
25. If the defamed party proves in court that the following circumstances occurred in the disclosure of matters involving the public interest specified in Article 24 of this Act, the court shall deem that the party accused of defamation is not entitled to the privilege afforded under that Article.

(a) The defamed party having requested the party accused of defamation to publish or disclose, together with a statement that the defamed party has made a statement or given information contradicting the information disclosed, or together with a further detailed explanation of that information to a reasonable extent, that information in that manner; and

(b) While so requested as specified in subsection (a) of this Article, the publication or disclosure of that information contrary thereto, or the information having been published or disclosed

[stamp] [signature]

in an unreasonable manner.

Chapter Five
Principles for Resolving Defamation Matters Outside Court

Remedies Available Prior to Bringing a Defamation Action
26. Before the defamed party brings an action under this Act against the party accused of defamation and submits the matter to court, the procedures set out in this Chapter may be completed in order to seek a remedy for that matter.

Giving Notice to the Party Accused of Defamation
27. (a) If a defamatory statement is made or such information is made public, the defamed party may give a notice to the party accused of defamation, in order to inform the party accused of defamation that it contains information carrying a defamatory meaning, or that a defamatory meaning is conveyed by the expressions contained therein, or that it refers to such a thing.

(b) The notice to the party accused of defamation under subsection (a) of this Article shall be sent in writing. And that notice shall include the following information.

(1) The place where the defamatory information was made public, or the means by which it can be accessed;

(2) The thing the defamed party alleges to be defamatory;

[stamp] [signature]

(3) That the statement or information is damaging to the reputation of the defamed party, and the damage suffered by that party; and

(4) The period given to indicate whether or not resolution of the matter is desired; the period so given shall be a period of not less than 7 (seven) days.

(c) If a notice has been sent under subsection (a) of this Article, a defamation action shall not be brought under Chapter Six of this Act before the expiry of the period specified in that notice. And if the party accused of defamation has not given a reply within the period specified in the notice so sent in writing, this Act shall not bar the bringing of a defamation action under Chapter Six of this Act.

Offer to Resolve the Matter
28. (a) If the party accused of defamation responds within the period stated in the notice sent in writing by the defamed party under Article 27 of this Act and wishes to resolve the matter, it may offer to act in one or more of the following ways.

(1) Making an appropriate correction to the information made public by way of defamation, or, if there is a particular defamatory meaning conveyed by or referred to in the expressions of that information, to that meaning;

(2) The party who defamed, in relation to the information made public, requesting, in an appropriate manner, from the defamed party

[stamp] [signature]

.

(b) An offer made under subsection (a) of this Article shall be made in writing. And that offer shall include the following matters.

(1) That the offer is an offer made by way of resolving the matter under this Chapter;

(2) That the offer is an offer open for acceptance by the party to whom the offer is addressed within the period specified in the offer;

(3) The defamatory statement or information made or given by the party who defamed to which the offer relates; and

(4) The manner proposed for implementing the matters contained in the offer.

(c) In circumstances where an offer is made under this Article to seek an apology from the defamed party, or, together with that, to publish information that an apology has been sought, it shall be done in a manner agreed by both parties.

(d) In circumstances where an offer is made under this Article to pay compensation for the damage suffered by the defamed party, the amount of money to be paid as compensation shall be determined in a manner agreed by both parties. And if agreement cannot be reached on the amount of money so determined to be paid,

[stamp] [signature]

that amount shall be determined by the court.

Withdrawal of the Offer
29. (a) The party who made an offer to resolve the matter under Article 28 of this Act has the option to withdraw that offer in writing before it is accepted by the party to whom the offer is addressed.

(b) Where the party who made the offer withdraws that offer under subsection (a) of this Article, this Act shall not bar the making of a fresh offer in accordance with Article 28 of this Act.

Acceptance of the Offer and Signing of the Agreement
30. (a) If the defamed party accepts an offer made by the party accused of defamation under Article 28 of this Act, both parties shall sign a written agreement setting out the manner agreed by both parties.

(b) The agreement specified in this Article shall be notarised through a public notary in accordance with Law No. 5/2019 (Legal Profession Act of the Maldives) and the relevant regulation made under that Act. And that agreement shall be deemed a valid agreement only if it has been notarised in accordance with this Article.

(c) If both parties sign an agreement to resolve the matter under subsection (a) of this Article, the principles set out in Article 31 of this Act shall apply.

[stamp] [signature]

(d) Where something defamatory was said or information was given by more than one party, and any one or some of those parties make an offer to resolve the matter with the defamed party under Article 28 of this Act, and the defamed party accepts it and signs an agreement under subsection (a) of this Article, this shall not affect the right afforded to the defamed party to file a defamation action under this Act against those parties among the parties accused of defamation who do not make an offer.

Consequence of Signing the Agreement
31. (a) If an agreement to resolve a defamation matter is signed under Article 30 of this Act, the right to bring a defamation action afforded to the defamed party under Article 31 of this Act may not be exercised.

(b) Notwithstanding subsection (a) of this Article, this Act shall not bar the submission to court of a matter concerning the enforcement of an agreement signed under Article 30 of this Act.

Chapter Six
Bringing a Defamation Action

Right to Bring a Defamation Action
32. (a) If an act of defamation is committed by any party, the defamed party has the right to bring a defamation action against the party who committed that act.

(b) The right to bring a defamation action under this Act

[stamp] [signature]

shall be afforded only to the defamed party.

(c) Notwithstanding subsection (b) of this Article, if the defamed party is a minor or a person in a circumstance in which he lacks the capacity to bring an action, this Act shall not bar the bringing of that action on behalf of that child or person.

Time Limit for Filing a Defamation Action and for Trial
33. A defamation action under this Act shall be brought before the expiry of 1 (one) year from the date on which the cause giving rise to the right to bring that action came into existence. And notwithstanding anything otherwise provided in another Act, the court shall decide on a defamation action under this Act within a maximum of 6 (six) months from the date on which that action is filed in court.

Parties Against Whom an Action Lies
34. (a) A defamation action may be brought only against the party or parties who made the defamatory statement, gave the information or wrote the writing.

(b) If the alleged defamation was through a writing or image printed publicly, in addition to the parties specified in subsection (a) of this Article, a defamation action may be brought against the parties who print, sell or distribute that writing or image, or display it for sale or for the purpose of making it public.

(c) If the alleged defamation was through a writing or information contained in a book, newspaper, magazine or other similar thing, and if the party who committed the defamatory act is not known, against the defamatory

[stamp] [signature]

writing or information: the owner of the book in which it was published, or the party operating the newspaper or magazine, or a party responsible for that thing, a defamation action may be brought.

Parties Against Whom an Action Cannot Be Brought
35. Bringing a defamation action against the following parties is not a matter permitted by this Act.

(a) The various institutions of the Government; and

(b) The independent commissions and offices of the State.

Determination of the Matter by the Court
36. In a defamation action, if it is proven to the court that an act of defamation has been committed in the manner set out in this Act, the court has the power to determine the following matters.

(a) Ordering the party who defamed to apologise, in an appropriate manner, to the defamed party in open court or in another manner determined by the court;

(b) Ordering an appropriate correction to be made to the information made public by way of defamation;

(c) Removing the information made public by way of defamation, or bringing to an end the making of it public;

(d) Determining the manner in which information that the party who defamed has apologised, or the correction made to the statement made or the information given in a defamatory manner, shall be announced or published

[stamp] [signature]

;

(e) Ordering the party who defamed to pay the defamed party compensation for the damage suffered as a result of defamation, in the manner determined in this Chapter.

Award of Compensation for Damage
37. (a) In a defamation action filed under this Act, if the claimant has suffered damage as a result of defamation, and the claimant has requested that compensation for that damage be awarded against the party who defamed, the court shall award compensation for damage in the manner set out in this Chapter.

(b) The court shall decide to award compensation for the damage which the claimant states it has suffered as a result of defamation only if, together with determining that an act of defamation of the claimant has been committed, the court is satisfied that the claimant has suffered damage in connection with that act of defamation, or that it is foreseeable that damage may be suffered.

Occurrence of Damage and Foreseeability of Damage
38. (a) The damage for which compensation may be awarded to the claimant as a result of defamation shall be damage actually suffered by that party and/or damage foreseeable, at the time the defendant made the defamatory statement or gave such information, as likely to be suffered by the claimant in the future.

[stamp] [signature]

(b) For the purposes of subsection (a) of this Article, "damage foreseeable as likely to be suffered" means that damage being deemed, when viewed from the perspective of a reasonable person, to be damage that may be suffered by the claimant.

Nature of Compensation
39. In defamation actions filed under this Act, the court shall award compensation for damage suffered as a result of defamation, in the manner requested by the claimant, of one of the following two types or of both types.

(a) If the claimant has suffered material damage as a result of defamation, compensation for that material damage;

(b) If the claimant has suffered moral damage as a result of defamation, compensation for that moral damage.

Amount of Compensation
40. (a) If the claimant has suffered material damage as a result of defamation, the compensation to be afforded for that damage shall, in a manner not inconsistent with subsection (b) of this Article, be financial compensation in an amount commensurate with the material damage suffered by that party as a result of defamation.

(b) In no circumstance shall the amount awarded by the court under subsection (a) of this Article as compensation for the material damage suffered by the claimant exceed 500,000 (five hundred thousand) Rufiyaa.

(c) The compensation to be afforded for the moral damage to the reputation of the claimant as a result of defamation shall be, having regard to the

[stamp] [signature]

severity of that damage, an amount between 50,000 (fifty thousand) Rufiyaa and 500,000 (five hundred thousand) Rufiyaa.

(d) In bringing an action to seek compensation for moral damage as specified in this Article, this Act does not require that material damage has been suffered.

Efforts to Mitigate Damage
41. (a) If, by way of resolving the defamation matter, the defendant has made an offer under Article 28 of this Act to seek an apology from the claimant and/or to pay compensation to that party, the court shall, in determining compensation for damage, take that into consideration, deeming that the defendant has made efforts to mitigate the damage suffered as a result of defamation.

(b) In the circumstance specified in subsection (a) of this Article, the court has the discretion to reduce the amount of compensation for damage to be afforded to the claimant as a result of defamation.

(c) In a matter submitted for the enforcement of an agreement signed under Article 30 of this Act to resolve a defamation matter, when the court determines an appropriate amount to be paid to the defamed party as compensation for damage suffered as a result of defamation, it shall take into consideration any measures taken to implement the matters contained in the agreement.

Formulation of Standards for Determining Compensation for Damage
42. For the purpose of the court determining, in a defamation action, the compensation for damage to be awarded to the claimant as a result of defamation,

[stamp] [signature]

detailed principles and standards relating to such matters shall be set out in the regulation made under this Act, in a manner not inconsistent with the standards set out in this Chapter. Accordingly, at a minimum, the following matters shall be determined in that regulation.

(a) The standard for identifying material and moral damage suffered, or foreseeable as likely to be suffered, as a result of defamation;

(b) The standard for assessing and calculating damage;

(c) The circumstances in which the court may decide to increase or reduce the amount to be awarded as compensation for damage suffered as a result of defamation, in determining that amount;

(d) The principles for differentiating the standard for calculating compensation for damage in circumstances where the claimant is a legal person.

Chapter Seven
Miscellaneous

Making of Regulations
43. (a) The regulations required to be made under this Act shall be made by the Attorney General's Office.

(b) The regulations required to be made under this Act shall be made and published in the Government Gazette within 30 (thirty) days of the commencement of this Act.

Regulations Repealed
44. Upon the commencement of this Act, the "Regulation on Awarding Compensation for Damage Suffered as a Result of Defamation", included in Schedule 2 of Law No. 6/2008 (General

[stamp] [signature]

Regulations Act), is hereby repealed.

Commencement of the Act
45. This Act shall commence from the date on which 30 (thirty) days have elapsed from the date on which this Act is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.

46. Unless the manner in which an expression or word is used in this Act specifically conveys a different meaning, the following expressions and words shall have the meanings given to them below.

(a) "Defamation" means the meaning given to that word in Article 9 of this Act.

(b) "Defamed party" means a party whose reputation has been harmed as a result of a statement made, information given or an act committed by a person. This includes natural persons and legal persons.

(c) "Party accused of defamation" or "party who defamed" means a party who makes a defamatory statement, or gives such information, in attribution to a particular person or a particular party.

(d) "Ill intent" means, with the aim of intentionally causing harm to a particular party, or of changing for the worse the way that party is regarded by other parties, or of insulting and demeaning that party, a statement

[stamp] [signature]

being made, or information being given, or an act being committed.

(e) "Without reasonable care" means things done without making efforts to a reasonable extent to ascertain the truth or falsity of the matter, when making a statement, giving information or committing any other act.

(f) "Public company" means any company that is not a private company, that has been granted permission to sell shares, or debentures and/or bonds, to the public, or that is seeking such permission, and that is incorporated or registered as a public company in accordance with Law No. 7/2023 (Companies Act).

(g) "Newspaper" means publications, whether under the name of daily newspapers, weekly newspapers, trade publications or any other name, published in the Maldives by print, the internet or other media means, available for purchase or available free of charge, for the purpose of disseminating information, news, opinion and advertisements to the public.

(h) "Book" means things made by binding written writings or blank pages together into a single volume, covered with a binding, and made so that it can be opened and closed. This definition includes all such things not deemed to be a newspaper, as well as writings, CDs, diskettes and modern means prepared for the provision of information

[stamp] [signature]

.

(i) "Media" means broadcast television and radio operated for the purpose of disseminating news, information, entertainment, opinion and advertisements to the public, cable television networks, and the delivery of content disseminated through any of these means via software, a website or an application operated through the internet; and daily newspapers, weekly newspapers, magazines and other similar publications delivering news, information and current affairs, published in print or published on software, a website or an application operated through the internet.

(j) "Magazine" includes writings and journals issued by publishing news, information and opinion based on academic, scientific and other various fields.
